claims.text: When wildChild is true, static children are tried via indices before falling back to the wildcard, so case-insensitive lookups prefer static routes over param routes.
The code comment's example is /PREFIX/XXX resolving to /prefix/xxx rather than matching :id.
The first child of a node with a wildcard is usually a static child, not the wildcard; addChild keeps the wildcard child last.
n.wildChild is set when the wildcard is added.
The fallback takes n.children[len(n.children)-1] as the wildcard child, with a comment saying it is always at the end of the array.
Insertion uses the same convention of keeping the wildcard child at the end.
Taking children[0] would pick a static child instead of the wildcard.
n.indices holds the first bytes of static children only; the wildcard has no entry there, so a separate step is needed to reach the wildcard child.
The static-child attempts are recursive calls that return nil on failure, and control then falls through to the wildcard, keeping the param route as a fallback.
Commit 472d086, "fix(tree): panic in findCaseInsensitivePathRec with RedirectFixedPath", introduced the static-first order.
The panic in the commit title is likely the failure case when the wildcard was handled without checking static children.
